Solve a Scoring Step From the Square-Root Design

Source: R/augmented.R
augmented_solve.Rd

Decomposes the augmented matrix \(A = [R;\, C]\), whose cross-product \(A'A = R'R + C'C\) is the penalized information, and returns the increment solving

$$(R'R + C'C)\,\delta = u$$

The augmented form never forms \(R'R\) or the penalized information, so a design with condition number \(\kappa\) is decomposed at \(\kappa\) and not at \(\kappa^2\), which the normal equations would give.

Usage

augmented_solve(R, C, u, how, threads = 1L, tol = NULL)

Arguments

R

The square-root design, as sqrt_design() returns it, \(nK \times p\).

C

The penalty's factor, as penalty_sqrt() returns it, with p columns and at most p rows. May have zero rows for an unpenalized model.

u

The right-hand side, a numeric vector of length p, or a matrix with p rows whose columns are solved with one factorization; delta is then a matrix of the same shape.

how

"qr" or "svd". "svd" has no sparse counterpart, so with how = "svd" a sparse pair is densified first.

threads

How many threads the triangular factor may use, a plain integer. With 1L the threaded route is not used.

tol

NULL for the defaults, or the tolerance of the decomposition: with how = "qr", the tolerance of the pivoted qr(), which is also the threshold of the equilibrated diagonal for the threaded route (default 1e-7); with how = "svd", the relative cut of the singular values (default \(\max(\dim A)\,\epsilon\)).

Value

A list with the elements delta, rank and dropped:

delta

the increment, an unnamed numeric vector of length p. It is zero in every coordinate that the pivoted route dropped.

rank

the rank used, an integer. It is always p on the threaded and sparse routes, which hand a deficient matrix to the dense route instead of reporting a smaller rank, and it is the number of retained singular values on the "svd" route.

dropped

the integer positions of the columns that the pivoted qr() route left out (the aliased coordinates); integer(0) on the sparse, threaded and "svd" routes.

The four routes

The routes are tried in this order.

  1. Sparse QR, when either factor is a Matrix object. The pair is passed to sparse_augmented_solve(), which returns NULL on a rank-deficient matrix.

  2. SVD, when how = "svd". The singular values below \(\max(\dim A)\,\epsilon\,\sigma_{\max}\) are dropped and the increment is built from the retained right singular vectors, so the solution of a deficient system is the minimum-norm one.

  3. The threaded triangular factor, when how = "qr", threads > 1 and \(m p^2\) is at least 5e7, where \(m\) is the number of rows of \(A\). Only the triangular factor is read, so a kernel that produces it without accumulating \(Q\) does the whole job.

  4. qr(), the pivoted LINPACK route, which returns a rank and can drop columns. A sparse solve that returned NULL continues here on densified factors.

Why the rank test is equilibrated

The threaded route is taken only where the matrix has full rank by a comfortable margin. The test reads the diagonal of the triangular factor divided by each column's norm. Writing \(T\) for the triangular factor of \(A\), so that \(A'A = T'T\), scaling the columns of \(A\) scales the diagonal of \(T\) by the same factors, so the ratio is the diagonal of a decomposition with unit column norms.

The raw diagonal would report a matrix as near-singular whenever its columns differ in size, and a large smoothing parameter produces that difference between the penalty rows of its own block and an unpenalized block. Scaling each column to unit norm removes differences in column size from any source and leaves an exact collinearity exactly singular.

The route is taken when the smallest equilibrated entry exceeds tol times the largest (1e-7 by default, the tolerance that dqrdc2 uses), so that a matrix that the pivoted route would call deficient is solved there and its rank is returned.

See also

sqrt_design() and penalty_sqrt() for the two factors, sparse_augmented_solve() for the sparse route.
